newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrials fall below key 10,000 level.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrials fall below key 10,000 level.

text.p: Zimbabwe industrial shares on Thursday slid below the key 10,000 point level but dealers said this was a temporary setback and fundamentals remained good.
"It's a little weaker and has fallen below the 10,000 mark, but the fundamentals are still strong. It's a temporary setback and everything is still looking good," one dealer said.
Dealers said industrials' 59.63 point fall to close at 9,972.25 was part of the market's correction and could also be that investors had yet to digest new issues.
They said players were now looking for bargains.

"It's a correction and we can still look forward to a good performance. People are looking at the market and waiting for bargains. There is still a lot of money that needs to find a home," another dealer said.
Barclays was knocked 100 cents to 32 dollars, Rothmans was bashed 1,000 cents to 50 dollars, Radar lost 60 cents to 400 cents and Alloys shed 50 cents to 650 cents.
But Meikles gained 50 cents to 2,150 cents, ZSR added 50 cents to 1,500 cents and Zimplow was up 50 cents to 675 cents.
The tiny seven-share mining index also took a heavy knock, cutting 35.63 points off to 913.38.
Falgold and Wankie traded at previous levels, while Bindura lost 50 cents to 700 cents, Falcon lost 50 cents to 1,200 cents and Rio Tinto fell 100 cents to 2,000 cents.
